rows: What defines a mass extinction?
Rate spike 10–100× background, affecting multiple major groups globally, within <3 Myr
Which extinction was worst?
End-Permian (P-T): ~90–96% of marine species, ~70% of terrestrial species lost
What caused the P-T extinction?
Siberian Traps LIP volcanism → CO₂ + warming + ocean anoxia + acidification cascade
What caused the End-Ordovician?
Gondwana glaciation → rapid cooling + sea level drop → habitat loss
What caused the Late Devonian?
Multi-causal: forest CO₂ drawdown → cooling + anoxia in shelf seas; no bolide needed
What caused the T-J extinction?
CAMP volcanism as Pangaea rifted; selectively killed pseudosuchians, not dinosaurs
Why is K-Pg the "most famous" but not the worst?
~40% genera lost (less than P-T at >70%) but icons like non-avian dinosaurs lost; best evidence
What traits predict survival in mass extinctions?
Small body, dietary generalism, wide geographic range, infaunal/burrowing, detritivory
How long do ecosystems take to recover?
5–20 Myr for full ecosystem recovery; some reef gaps last 10+ Myr
Is there a 6th extinction?
Yes by rate metrics (100–1000× background); not yet at Big Five severity but trajectory is alarming
